data.narrative:
Oklo is a public-stage nuclear energy company valued at $7.0B following its market listing. The target operates within a nuclear energy sector comprising three public comparables (OKLO, NNE, SMR) and five private peers including X-Energy, Nano Nuclear Energy, Fuse Energy, NuScale Power, and Terrestrial Energy.

The peer-median method is not applicable to this valuation. The nuclear energy sector contains only three public companies total, and filtering for same-stage, adjacent-stage, or similar-valuation-tier peers yields fewer than three datapoints in each category. Applying an all-sector median would conflate disparate business models and development timelines, introducing material bias. No triangulation across multiple quantitative methods could therefore be completed using the available dataset.

The analysis is constrained by the nascent and heterogeneous nature of the advanced nuclear market. Oklo's $7.0B public valuation reflects investor sentiment and market pricing rather than support from traditional comparable-company analysis. Key uncertainties include the wide variance in technology readiness across peers (from preclinical to demonstration-stage), regulatory pathway risk specific to microreactor deployment, and the absence of revenue generation across the peer set. Further valuation work would require either expansion of the comparable universe, introduction of precedent transaction data, or cash-flow-based modeling tied to deployment milestones.
